title: Design, acceptance and notes never reach GitHub
description: Only title, description (issue body) and the close reason sync. design, acceptance_criteria and notes stay local; e.g. nassau-949.2 / issue #25 has acceptance text only in the bead. Sync each as one marked comment (<!-- bd-comment:notes -->, :design, :acceptance; the existing import already skips bd-comment markers), created when the field first becomes non-empty and edited in place via PATCH /issues/comments/{id}. Identity is the stored comment id, not position, so comments from others in between do not matter. Store comment id and last-synced text per bead field (watcher state and server kv). Reconcile with a three-way compare (bead, GitHub, last synced): one side changed wins; both changed keeps the bead value and preserves the GitHub text as a plain 'Overwritten GitHub edit' comment. GitHub edits arrive via issue_comment.edited and update the bead field. Replaces bd-gh-sync-pft.9.

title: Nest imported beads under parents beyond the 24h fresh window
description: nest_fresh only renames beads recorded in the fresh map for 24h. A sub-issue attached later, or moved to another parent, keeps a non-dotted or wrong-parent ID. Nest any auto-shaped ID whose parent-child edge disagrees with its prefix.

title: Close-reason classification matches substrings in free text
description: state_reason_for uses contains() on 'invalid', 'duplicate', "won't", so 'Fixed the invalid-cache bug' becomes not_planned and 'Removed duplicate code' becomes duplicate. Match only exact/leading keywords; everything else is completed.

title: Apply issue field events from the payload
description: issues.edited/labeled/unlabeled/assigned/unassigned/closed/reopened still go through bd github pull. Apply title, body, labels, assignee, state and state_reason from the payload via bd update. Needs bd's label vocabulary (type::, priority::<name>, status::) confirmed; keep bd github pull as fallback for unknown labels. Closed events must still resolve a 'close with comment' within the batch.

title: Commit, release and verify payload-driven comments and relations on nassau
description: Comment (created/edited/deleted) and sub_issues/issue_dependencies events are applied from the payload (Mode::Events, scoped relations scan). Cut v0.1.4, deploy, then on nassau add/edit/delete a comment and add/remove a sub-issue and blocked-by; confirm the server log shows 'queued N change(s)' with no GraphQL full scan or bd github pull. Confirm the sub_issues/issue_dependencies payload keys (parent_issue, sub_issue, blocked_issue, blocking_issue) against a live delivery.

title: Drive the sync from webhook payloads and harden bidirectional sync
description: Consume GitHub webhook payloads directly instead of re-querying the API, ignore events we caused, and fix the correctness/efficiency gaps found in the bidirectional sync review. Payload comments and relation events are implemented (uncommitted, v0.1.4 candidate); the children are the remaining work.

title: Cut the first release (v0.1.0)
description: The Action and scripts/install-bd-gh-sync.sh now only download release binaries (no cargo fallback), so nothing works until a v* tag exists. Tag v0.1.0 after the Rust port is committed, check release.yml builds linux-x86_64/aarch64 (musl) and macos-aarch64, then run the beads-sync workflow once.

title: Webhook receiver for GitHub→beads (replace the Actions path)
description:
Actions adds ~60s debounce + ~25s job per sync and cannot receive sub_issues, issue_dependencies or projects_v2_item events. Run an always-on service (mini PC or small VM) that receives GitHub webhooks, applies them to its own beads clone (reuse gh-to-beads.sh logic) and bd dolt pushes within ~1-2s.
Design questions: public HTTPS ingress for a home box (Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale Funnel, smee.io relay, or a VM with a public IP); webhook secret verification (X-Hub-Signature-256); repo webhook vs GitHub App (App also enables bd-gh-sync-pft.10 and project scopes); short in-process debounce/batching; catch-up after downtime (keep the since-watermark reconcile, maybe the 6h Action as a safety net); serialising writes to the Dolt clone; packaging (systemd unit / container).
close_reason: Webhook server shipped as bd-gh-sync server; whole tool ported to Rust (sync, watch, server), release workflow, deploy/ files, README

title: Verify relation/assignee/comment endpoints against real GitHub
description: Tests use tests/fake_github.py. Exercise sub_issues, dependencies/blocked_by, assignees PATCH and the GraphQL relations query (GITHUB_TOKEN issues:read) on the real repo after pushing.

title: Sync assignees GitHub↔beads
description: Map GitHub assignees to bead assignee and back.

title: Sync comments GitHub↔beads
description: Import issue comments via bd comments add with a marker; watcher posts new bead comments to GitHub.

title: Sync relationships GitHub↔beads
description: Sub-issues ↔ parent-child deps, blocked_by ↔ blocks deps, both directions.

title: Debounced, watermark-based GitHub→beads sync
description: Debounce job (cancel-in-progress) + sync job pulling issues updated since a bd kv watermark; also fix the dolt pull that fails on uncommitted bootstrap changes.

title: Batch GitHub→beads sync and sync comments, relationships, assignees both ways
description: Each issue event runs its own ~25s Action; comments, sub-issues/dependencies and assignees do not sync.

title: Limit webhook body size and rate
description: DefaultBodyLimit is 25 MB, so an unauthenticated caller can make the server read 25 MB before the signature fails. Lower the limit on /webhook to about 1 MB (GitHub allows up to 25 MB but issue/comment events are far smaller; check the largest observed delivery first) and add a rate limit for failed signatures in Caddy (or per IP in the server). Log rejected deliveries with the source address.

title: Reject replayed webhook deliveries
description: A captured signed delivery is accepted again and triggers a sync. Reject replays: remember recent X-GitHub-Delivery IDs (bounded set, shared with bd-gh-sync-2s6.4 dedupe) and refuse payloads whose issue/comment updated_at is older than the last applied (see bd-gh-sync-2s6.5). Return 200 without queueing for a known delivery so GitHub does not retry.

title: Add a bd-gh-sync verify command
description: Compare every linked bead with its GitHub issue and print drift (title, state, labels, assignee, relations, missing comments). Useful as an e2e check and to close bd-gh-sync-ser.

title: Skip the wasted first push of GitHub-pulled beads
description: A pulled bead has no pushed.json entry, so the watcher pushes it back and can overwrite a newer GitHub edit. GET the issue first and, if it matches the bead fingerprint, record it and skip the push.

title: Do not remove relations when GraphQL pages are truncated
description: blockedBy(first:100), timelineItems(first:100) and closedByPullRequestsReferences(first:10) are not paginated; a truncated node makes plan_relations remove edges that exist. Skip removals for nodes that report hasNextPage.

title: pull_request events without a full scan
description: pull_request webhooks queue Job::SinceLast and a full relations scan. Resolve the issues a PR closes (closingIssuesReferences on that PR) and sync only those.

title: Ignore events we caused (sender filter)
description: Drop events whose sender is the sync identity. Today the watcher and server use the user's PAT so they are indistinguishable; needs the GitHub App identity (bd-gh-sync-pft.10). Until then idempotent state comparison is the guard.

title: Deduplicate webhook deliveries by X-GitHub-Delivery
description: Keep a bounded set of recent delivery IDs in the worker so redeliveries and retries are not applied twice.

title: Order events by updated_at / ignore stale payloads
description: Two quick events can arrive out of order. Record the last applied updated_at per issue and skip payloads older than it.

title: Create beads from issues.opened with the short ID directly
description: Use bd create --id <short> --external-ref <url> from the opened payload so new issues never get a long timestamp ID and the rename step (shorten_imports) becomes a fallback only. Depends on the field mapping child.

title: Cut bd invocations per sync
description: A webhook-triggered sync takes ~4-5s, almost all in bd/Dolt (bootstrap, dolt commit/pull, 5x bd export, kv, dolt push). Reuse exports within a pass, skip bootstrap for an already-bootstrapped server clone, and measure. Webhook-to-Dolt latency is otherwise ~1s debounce + this.
close_reason: Cached unchanged exports within sync passes, skipped bootstrap for initialized embedded Dolt clones, and added command/pass timing logs.

title: Handle bead deletion and issue transfer/deletion
description: Deleting a bead leaves its issue open; transferring or deleting an issue leaves a stale bead. Proposed: bead deleted → close issue as not_planned; issue transferred → update the bead's external_ref; issue deleted → close or flag the bead.
close_reason: Bead deletion closes the issue not_planned; deleted/transferred issues relink or flag the bead; verified against this repo

title: Linked pull requests drive bead status
description: A PR that says Fixes/Closes #N: on open set the bead to in_progress and add a comment with the PR link; on merge GitHub closes the issue and the normal sync closes the bead. Needs pull_request events.
close_reason: Open linked PRs set the bead in_progress with a PR comment; verified against this repo (merge path is the normal close sync)

title: Import issue cross-references as related dependencies
description: Mentions like 'Ref: #4' show up as cross-referenced timeline events. Import them as related (or relates-to) bead links, GitHub→beads only (beads has no mention concept). Needs the timeline API per updated issue.
close_reason: Cross-references imported as related deps via GraphQL timelineItems; verified against this repo

title: Sync close reason (state_reason ↔ bead close reason)
description: GitHub closes carry state_reason completed / not_planned / duplicate; bd close --reason stores free text. Pull: set the bead close reason from state_reason. Push: close as not_planned when the bead's reason says won't-do / not planned.
notes: Tests dropped by decision (see AGENTS.md Testing)
close_reason: Close reason syncs both ways via state_reason; e2e covered

title: Broaden GitHub↔beads sync coverage
description: Follow-ups to bd-gh-sync-n7w: fields and events that still don't sync, and moving GitHub→beads off Actions.

title: Per-repo webhook secrets
description: One WEBHOOK_SECRET covers every registered repo. Anyone holding it can forge events for any repo, and the payload-applied path (comments, relation edges) writes payload data straight into beads. Generate a secret per repo (store in the project dir or Dolt kv, never in the repo), register it with the webhook in 'server add', and verify with the secret of the repo named in the payload (look it up before verifying, using X-GitHub-Hook-Installation-Target or a per-repo URL path such as /webhook/owner/name). Migrate existing webhooks via 'server add'. Until then keep the reconcile scan as the correction path.

title: Prevent duplicate comments from multiple watchers
description: push_comments and post_close_reason check-then-post, so two machines can both post. Elect one pusher, or delete duplicates carrying our marker after posting.

title: Test a server rename racing a local edit
description: Edit a bead locally while the server renames it and check what bd dolt pull does (merge conflict handling). Currently untested.

title: Always advance the server's since cursor after a successful pass
description: sync_github only stores since when something changed, so on a quiet repo every pass re-lists all issues updated since the last change.

title: Post watcher comments as a GitHub App
description: Comments the watcher posts appear under the token owner. A GitHub App could post as 'beads-sync' and name the bead author in the text.

title: Sync GitHub Projects (v2) fields
description: Project fields (Status, Priority, Iteration, Estimate) ↔ bead status/priority/estimate. Needs a token with project scope (not GITHUB_TOKEN); projects_v2_item events need an org-level webhook or App, so only practical with the webhook receiver (else polling).
close_reason: Added opt-in GitHub Projects v2 field reconciliation for status, priority, estimate, and iteration/defer; added separate token, webhook handling, publish paths, and setup documentation.

title: Map supersede/duplicate to GitHub close-as-duplicate
description: bd supersede / supersedes links ↔ GitHub 'duplicate of #N'. First confirm GitHub's API for the duplicate link.
close_reason: Duplicate/supersedes mapped both ways (GraphQL closeIssue duplicateIssueId, Issue.duplicateOf); verified against this repo

title: Sync comment edits and deletions
description: Only comment creation syncs (both ways). Edits/deletes on GitHub or beads are not propagated; bd has no comment edit/delete, and GitHub comment ids would need tracking.
close_reason: GitHub comment edits/deletes arrive as append-only bead notes (bd has no comment edit/delete); verified against this repo

title: Move bead-to-GitHub pushes to the server (design)
description: Server already has the Dolt clone and token: poll git ls-remote origin refs/dolt/data, pull on change, run the watcher's push logic. Removes per-machine watchers and duplicate pushers at the cost of latency. Check whether GitHub push webhooks fire for refs/dolt/*.

title: Design / acceptance / notes on GitHub
description: beads fields with no GitHub counterpart. Marked body sections would fight bd's own push, which treats the whole body as the description; would need splitting/rebuilding the body on both sides. Low priority unless wanted.

title: Native GitHub issue types ↔ bead type
description: Org-level issue types (Bug/Feature/Task) instead of type:: labels. Only applies to organisation repos; personal repos don't have them.

title: Milestones ↔ bead defer/due dates
description: Closest GitHub match for bd defer --until is a milestone due date, but milestones are shared buckets, not per-issue dates. Decide on a mapping before building.
